newsitem.title: HUNGARY: COCA-COLA TO INVEST FURTHER IN HUNGARY, EAST EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: COCA-COLA TO INVEST FURTHER IN HUNGARY, EAST EUROPE.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co will probably invest $50 million in Hungary in 1997 as a part of the company's expansion in the Eastern part of Europe, Coca-Cola Chairman Doug Ivester said on Tuesday.

Ivester was quoted by the Hungarian daily Vilaggazdasag as saying that Coca-Cola is likely to invest the funds in sales development and could boost the staff of its Hungarian subsidiary by up to 300 new employees.
Coca-Cola has already invested $1.5 billion in the countries of Central Eastern Europe, of which Hungary took out $250 million, Vilaggazdasag said.
The report added that Coca-Cola also plans to invest one billion dollars in the Eastern part of Europe, including $100 million in both Russia and Poland in 1997.
Ivester was quoted as saying that Coca-Cola has recently become beverage market-leader in Russia and is also market-leader in Poland and Hungary.
